class: A frontend module that Playwright specs import in plain Node (directly or through its static import chain) gains an import through the bundler's path alias ('@/...'); the bundler and the unit runner resolve the alias, Node does not, so every e2e spec in the run fails at load while lint, unit tests and the build stay green.
mechanism: Row 23b added `import { isSuperseded } from '@/lib/newestWins'` to frontend/src/services/api.js. e2e/responsive.spec.ts imports src/router/routes.js, whose chain reaches src/lib/orderPath.js -> src/services/api.js; Playwright's loader has no '@' alias, so the run stopped with "Cannot find package '@/lib' imported from .../frontend/src/services/api.js". Every other module on that chain already used relative imports.

first_seen.where: CI App tests run 40077253832 on build/seq-chunk-2 49fe0462 (row 23b merged), job frontend
first_seen.evidence: Playwright: Error: Cannot find package '@/lib' imported from /home/runner/work/OptionsForOptions2/OptionsForOptions2/frontend/src/services/api.js; api, execute-screen-e2e and the kit CI green. The 23b builder and both checkers ran lint + targeted vitest + the DB-free pytest set; none runs Playwright locally (CI only).

fix: Instance: the import in api.js made relative (commit 3e340275). Class-level (2026-10-26): frontend/tests/e2e-node-import-closure.test.js walks the static import closure from every e2e file and playwright.config.js into src and fails on any '@/' specifier, failing closed on an unresolvable relative import, a static non-js/ts import or a computed import()/require(). Measured on origin/main 0e3bd2a1: 7 src files reached (execute, routes, nav, orderPath, api, newestWins, dataHealthText), 0 with an '@/' import; `playwright test --list` loads all 290 tests in 25 files.

detection.note: Vitest check in the normal frontend test job. Red proof: '@/lib/x' appended to src/lib/execute.js made the real-tree test fail naming the file; green on the clean tree. Blind spots: runtime-built imports, a package.json imports map or tsconfig paths that would make Node resolve '@/'. A lazy import('./X.vue') is not followed.
